cases.proves_bugs: BUG-223 (CDEDIT branch: the window words, the save and the reopen). The CD not-drawn-first branch and the "Flow:" line of the New Pipe window are not read (the New Pipe window dump on 3.0.88 holds no "Flow:" text).
cases.title: Edit Pipe on a pipe between two open ends: typing the levels the other way round makes the window name the first box Downstream and say the levels fall from point 2 to point 1; Save turns the arrow with no uphill line, and reopening shows the same
cases.plan_item: BUG-proof wave 1, group E (Edit Pipe, flow direction); BUG-223
cases.expected: CD from 150000,-90000 to 170000,-90000 with 18.000 then 17.800: the arrow reads rotation 0. CDEDIT: at first open the first box is named Upstream and there is no "levels fall" note. Type 17.800 in the first box and 18.000 in the second: the first box is now named Downstream, the second Upstream, the note reads "The levels fall from point 2 to point 1; CE records that as the flow direction." and the old note "Upstream invert is lower than downstream" is absent. Save: "Pipe updated.", no command-line line contains "flows uphill", and the arrow turns (rotation about 3.14). CDEDIT again: the first box reads 17.800 and is named Downstream, the second reads 18.000, the note is still there; Cancel without saving closes it. No CE window is left open and the drawing file on disk is unchanged.
cases.why_not_unit: The box names and the note are what the live Edit Pipe window shows on top of the real drawing; the save and the arrow are the live CDEDIT write.
not_automated: The schedule row of a pipe with two open ends (From IL 18.00 -> To IL 17.80) is not read: two open ends give no pit row in the Pit Schedule. The arrow picture is a Codex look (the robot reads only the arrow block's rotation).
Tim's step "CDEDIT again with 18.00 / 18.00: nothing is reversed" is NOT driven: a level pipe is flatter than 1 in 100 and opens the Grade mismatch window on 3.0.87 and later.

cases.proves_bugs: BUG-210 (one pipe end, a copied lone pit, Edit Pit and CDCHECK read at once; the Pit Schedule cells and the six-pipe junction are not driven)
cases.title: ERASE pit P8, COPY a lone pit onto its spot: the copy is linked to the pipe end at once (CDCHECK connections back, Edit Pit lists the pipe)
cases.plan_item: Bug-proof plan wave 1 (BUG_PROOF_PLAN_31OCT.md), group P: erase then copy onto the junction
cases.expected: After SETUP-R47v, a lone pit is placed at 150000,-70000 (CDCHECK Problems still reads '189 connections: 184 Connected, 1 Possible, 4 Unresolved, 0 Not Connected, 0 Unknown.'). ERASE of P8 says '1 pipe now has an end that is Not connected yet' and CDCHECK reads '188 connections: 183 Connected'. COPY of the lone pit by 0,-10000 puts one new pit block at 150000,-80000 (within 1 mm) and says '1 pit copied and numbered as new'. Straight after, with no other command, CDCHECK reads '189 connections: 184 Connected, 1 Possible, 4 Unresolved, 0 Not Connected, 0 Unknown.' again, and Edit Pit (PITEDIT) on the copy lists the pipe as LEAVING and never says 'The pit has no recorded connection to this pipe.'; Cancel closes it. No CE window is left open and the drawing file on disk is unchanged.
cases.why_not_unit: The link is made when AutoCAD ends the native COPY command and CE's clone reconcile runs on the live drawing.
not_automated: The Pit Schedule FROM / inlet / outlet cells for the copy are not read (the schedule needs its own window route); the six-pipe junction of the bug report and U after the copy are not driven.

DERIVED: the CDCHECK totals with the lone pit (no connection added by a pit with no pipes), and the role word LEAVING in Edit Pit. The copy's number is NOT asserted (it may take P8 back or the next free number): it is recorded from the PITEDIT dump.

cases.proves_bugs: BUG-234 (MOVE branch, and the one-end branch by a typed STRETCH; the real grip drag and the Pit Schedule rows are not driven)
cases.title: A flat pipe P91 to P92 MOVEd onto pits P93 and P94 records P93 to P94; its east end STRETCHed onto P92 then records P93 to P92
cases.plan_item: Bug-proof plan wave 1 (BUG_PROOF_PLAN_31OCT.md), group P: relink after MOVE or an end move
cases.expected: Four pits P91 to P94 and a flat 225 mm pipe P91 to P92 (both levels 18.000, no window). MOVE of the pipe alone by 0,-6000: the Civil log says 'Pipe endpoints updated: <pipe> from=P93 to=P94' and Edit Pipe shows 'Flow: P93 -> P94' with no P91 or P92 anywhere. STRETCH of the pipe's east end 6 m north onto P92: the log says 'Pipe endpoints updated: <pipe> from=P93 to=P92' and Edit Pipe shows 'Flow: P93 -> P92' with no P94. Both IL texts still read IL 18.000. Edit Pipe is closed with Cancel each time; no CE window is left open and the drawing file on disk is unchanged.
cases.why_not_unit: The pipe record is rewritten by CE's relink when AutoCAD ends the native MOVE and STRETCH commands on the live drawing.
not_automated: The real grip drag of an end (the bug's 'grip one end from P2 onto P3') is replaced by a typed STRETCH of that end; the Pit Schedule FROM / TO cells of P91 to P94 and U after each step are not driven.

DERIVED: that the four hand-typed numbers P91 to P94 are free in DRV1_B1 (it holds P1 to P10 by the R19 / R34 / N71 notes); if CE renumbers a pit the 'from=P93' checks fail first and the numbers are in the recorded Edit Pipe dumps.

cases.title: CDFALLSUGGEST: Enter at "Next level ... or Enter to finish" ends the command and states the count; no "Invalid point"
cases.expected: CDFALLSUGGEST, typed point 150000,-98000, Enter at the level question (skipped: 'No level at this point'), Enter at 'Next level (0 placed, 1 skipped), or Enter to finish:'. The command ends on that Enter and says 'CDFALLSUGGEST finished. 0 placed, 1 skipped.' inside the typed result; no 'Invalid point' anywhere; no FALL block is added; the drawing file on disk is unchanged.
cases.why_not_unit: The unit test proves the prompt options allow an empty answer; only live AutoCAD shows that a real Enter at that prompt ends the command instead of AutoCAD's own 'Invalid point.'.
not_automated: Accept a suggested arrow and then Enter (needs a point with a known level uphill of a grated pit with a known cover level; the fixture's levels near P4 are not read here). Esc at the same prompt is the old way out and is not the subject.
